title: Suspended Loads and Multiple Lifts
summary: Steel hangs over heads, and sometimes several beams ride one hook. This talk covers OSHA's rules for working under loads and for multiple lifts.
talking_points: Routes for suspended loads must be pre-planned so that no one has to work directly under a suspended load, except those making the initial connection of the steel and those hooking or unhooking the load (29 CFR 1926.753(d)(1)).

When people do work under a suspended load, materials must be rigged to prevent unintentional displacement, hooks with self-closing safety latches or equivalent must be used, and a qualified rigger must rig all loads (1926.753(d)(2)).

A multiple lift is allowed only if a multiple lift rigging assembly is used, no more than five members are hoisted, only beams and similar structural members are lifted, and all employees involved are trained (1926.753(e)(1)).
The crane must not be used for a multiple lift if that is contrary to the manufacturer's specifications and limitations (1926.753(e)(1)(v)).

Rigging assembly components must be designed for a maximum capacity for the total assembly and each attachment point, certified by the manufacturer or a qualified rigger, with a 5 to 1 safety factor (1926.753(e)(2)). The total load must stay within the crane load charts and rigging rating charts (1926.753(e)(3)).
Members must be attached at their center of gravity, kept reasonably level, rigged from the top down and at least 7 feet apart (1926.753(e)(4)).
Set members from the bottom up, and use controlled load lowering whenever the load is over the connectors (1926.753(e)(5)-(6)).
Employees who do multiple lift rigging must be trained in the hazards of multiple lifts and the proper procedures and equipment (1926.761(c)(1)).
site_hazards_to_check: People standing under the load path
Rigging not designed for multiple lifts
More than five members on one assembly
Members out of level or hung too close together
Untrained riggers on a multiple lift
discussion_questions: Who decides the load path, and how do we keep people out from under it?
Do we have a certified multiple lift assembly, and where is the certification?
How do we signal controlled lowering over the connectors?
